The Yield to Maturity not only takes into account the interest earned on bonds, but also any difference between the face value at maturity and the current market price.

For example, a 7% bond that matures in 1 year has a 7% yield if it is trading at par (100); but it yields just over 10% if it is trading at a price of 97, since you will also earn a 3-point gain when it matures at 100 (face value) a year later.
